subject: Medix AI — Deployment hardening & VPC isolation options (post-demo)
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@medix.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: Phil Johnson <phil.johnson@medix.ai>, Medix AI Security <security@medix.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 14:03:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up from demo — network isolation and SOC 2 questions

Thanks for the demo earlier, Logan — good overview. A few items from our side that we want to document and prioritize: 

1) SOC 2 status: We need a copy of Redwood's most recent SOC 2 report or an alternative attestation.
2) Data residency / GDPR: Can you confirm if Redwood hosts EU-only regions and whether customer data can be restricted to EU-only? Any data export controls we should be aware of?
3) Deployment topology: We're evaluating a VPC-attached deployment behind our private peering vs. a fully air-gapped on-prem option. Phil (CTO) will be particularly concerned about egress controls and network zones.
4) Vendor security questionnaire: attaching the initial questionnaire (see attached). Please have your security team start the intake and let us know an expected turnaround window.

Immediate asks:
- High-level diagram that maps where model weights and inference traffic sit in the VPC-attached flow (we need network zones labeled).
- Whether KV cache/prefix caches can be disabled for on-prem/isolated runs.

Can you confirm who from Redwood's security should own the questionnaire? We'd ideally have a first pass back in 5 business days.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Ruiz
Head of Product
Medix AI

Subject: Re: Follow-up from demo — network isolation and SOC 2 questions

Elena — thanks for the clear list and the questionnaire. Looping in Mina (security lead) and Karthik (solutions) to start the intake and map out a recommended architecture. Quick answers up front: 

- SOC 2: We can provide a SOC 2 Type II report under NDA; Mina will share the access workflow.
- EU regions: Redwood runs EU regions with data residency controls; we support restricting model state and logs to specific regions.
- On disabling caches: there are modes to reduce or disable prefix/KV caching for private deployments, but there are trade-offs for latency/cost. We'll document the options.

Next steps I propose: 
1) Mina to respond with SOC 2 delivery steps and initial questionnaire owner + ETA.
2) Karthik to produce a concise VPC-attached diagram (2 versions: peered VPC and air-gapped on-prem) and note where model binaries and KV cache live.
3) Internal sync: I will schedule a 30-min technical review for later this week (please share your availability).

Mina/Karthik — can you pick up the questionnaire and the diagram? Target: first pass in 5 business days as requested.

Best,
Logan
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up from demo — network isolation and SOC 2 questions

Hi Elena — thanks for the questionnaire and the list. I've started the intake and assigned sections to our control owners. Quick plan and clarifications: 

- SOC 2: We can provide a SOC 2 Type II report; we typically deliver it through a secure share after an NDA. Please confirm the right contact to send the access link to (security@medix.ai is fine).
- Vendor questionnaire: I've completed the high-level vendor answers and flagged a few items that need architecture input (encryption key custody, egress restrictions, and on-prem HSM options). Expect a marked-up xlsx back by 2026-11-16 EOD.
- EU residency: We have EU-only hosting available. For strict GDPR-only controls we recommend a dedicated VPC in eu-west-1 or an on-prem deployment.
- Caching controls: For dedicated/private deployments we can run in a "no-persist" cache mode (no long-term KV storage) which reduces leak surface; for truly air-gapped installs there is an on-prem package that keeps all data behind customer firewalls. Note: no-persist mode increases per-request GPU work and may raise latency/cost.

Action items we've taken: 
- Karthik is producing two simplified topology diagrams (peered VPC flow + air-gapped on-prem).
- I've created a short answers sheet for the questionnaire and attached it to this reply.
- I'm proposing a 30-min technical review on Thu 11/12 or Fri 11/13; please share best slots.

Deliverables we will provide:
- Annotated topology diagrams (PDF) showing model weight location, inference traffic paths, and recommended security controls.
- Marked-up vendor questionnaire (xlsx).
- SOC 2 delivery steps and NDA link.

Regards,
Mina Haddad
Security Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_vpc_patterns_v1.pdf (pdf), medix_network_zones_v1.pdf (pdf)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@medix.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 09:17:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up from demo — network isolation and SOC 2 questions

Elena / team — attaching the two topology sketches we discussed: 1) VPC-attached (peered) flow with labeled subnets/zones and 2) air-gapped on-prem pattern with HSM option. Highlights and recommendations: 

- VPC-attached: place inference servers in a private subnet behind customer-managed NAT; use prefix isolation for KV caches; lock egress via firewall rules to only approved update endpoints and metrics sinks. Recommend using customer KMS for key custody.
- Air-gapped: full on-prem install; model files loaded via signed artifacts; runtime in an isolated VLAN; HSM for key operations; no external telemetry unless explicitly allowed (we provide a one-way log export option to a mounted drive).

I've included estimated effort: VPC-attached validation (2–3 days), air-gapped evaluation and install plan (2–3 weeks depending on procurement and access).

Next: I'll upload the PDFs to the Drive link and return the completed questionnaire sections flagged for product/security input.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
